posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
The artwork on Temporal Event in Silver Gulch makes me giggle every time I look at it. The combo of Wraith's cartoony bug-eyed face and Argent's dejected staring contest with a lizard is delightfully absurd.

Construct Cataclysm, for being Badass Hilarious and showing how British Captain Cosmic is.

Haka of Shielding is another card with delightfully absurd art.  It's the balloon that really makes it.

Everything with Idealist on it. Especially her foil incap for her original version.

Setback's entire deck is great, but I especially like the flavor text for High Risk Behavior. "Oh, hello there! Have you considered, say, not hitting me?"

Aquatic Correspondence. :D That poor eel...

I am sad Unity won't have any more canon bots, because I want to see what her quips would be for all the other heroes' expies.

Tactics has a lot of funny cards, too. Bunker complaining that Wraith stole his foam grenades, Citizen Spring being all a-gosh at how violent Beacon is, Wraith complaining that AZ got her making cheesy ice puns...

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Okay, but Driving Mantis. 1's and 2's are pretty common area damage levels, so it turns Mr. Fixer into both a defensive and offensive powerhouse. I mean, yeah, you could do more damage with Grease Monkey Fist and Dual Crowbars, but that's just on your turn! Driving Mantis is for messing with the villains, making them beat up on Greazer's hair so he beats them back. (It's so much more satisfying than just having a villain target hit itself!)

To illustrate the point, starting with that card made games against Agent of Gloom Spite and Miss Information super-easy today. He almost single-handedly tore them apart with their own retaliation damage. (With a major assist from Visionary in Spite's case!)

I realized one of my favorite cards today is Wrecking Uppercut, from KNYFE’s deck. It just fits the theme so well, and feels so satisfying, (especially with the actual cards) that she hits a villain so hard they lose the top card of their deck.

And then the flavor text is hilarious too, because she’s getting fed up with Fright Train’s pun train! (About Trains)

Especially taken juxtaposed with Ambuscade's Personal Cloaking Device, because that card is set up to have Ambuscade as a Predator-esque merciless hunter stalking unsuspecting prey, then Haka of Shielding shows the prey is still unsuspecting because he didn't even notice the actual attack.

posts.name: Trajector

I was just thinking about how some cards manage to get the perfect combination of mechanics + theme.

Like the Shinobi Assassin: ninjas are more dangerous when you CAN’T see them than when you can!

Or the power on the Staff of Ra: chuck a priceless artifact at your foes!

Best of all, though, is Consider the Price of Victory. Baron Blade starts monologuing (“He starts MONOLOGUING!”) and the heroes take Sonic damage.

posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked: I like how Grenade Launcher follows the trope of not looking back at the explosion.  Retcon akways makes me chuckle having with Guise just inserting himself into Wraith's history.

posts.name: darkroydante
posts.cooked:
I just want to play the Harpy's deck very badly.

Until then, my single favorite card is probably High Risk Behvaiour. The art, flavor text, and game text are all great. Adjusting one token at the start of the turn can really set up some impressive plays, but more often than not I just add another token to fuel the High Risk-Looking Up combo. 

My favorite villain card is Losing To The Odds. I think it's fantastic that one of the longest player discussions I've ever been a part of in SotM was figuring out exactly how to get Ra to hit Nightmist and Fixer to exact HP values to win the game, which involved Nightmist redirecting damage to Fixer and other silliness.
